trickyParts: nats-server 2.10 accepts an update of a push durable's filter to EMPTY and then delivers nothing; the policy therefore sets FilterSubject '>' (regression test TestADurableFilteredOnTheStreamSubjectsDeliversEverySubjectOnceCorrected).

Node loss: the server keeps the dead connection's interest, so messages pushed to it in the last AckWait come back after newer ones. A one-AckWait wait before subscribing (architect Q2's wording) kept order only for SIGKILL; the new holder now subscribes at once, holds what it receives for AckWait + 1 s and delivers it sorted by stream sequence.
A renewal whose reply is lost but which landed made the next renewal conflict with the holder's own write; the lease now recognises its own boot and keeps the lease.
The lease runs on its own NATS connection; a ledger call cut by that connection's reconnect waits up to 5 s for it before the 30 s NAK (a 2 s blip had cost 25-30 s).
The standby's reconnect lines: tests count only the main client's reconnect (mainClientReconnects), since the lease connection logs the same message.
deviations: Architect Q1 (2026-10-27): a listener without the envoy_listener grant does not exit; it logs one ERROR naming the bucket and grant, receives only while the durable is not push-bound by another subscriber (no lease), uses per-process ledger/last-seen/grace, and /healthz reports lease unavailable.

Architect Q2: a hard take-over (SIGKILL, node loss) keeps per-session order and takes about 12 s (test bound 15 s) instead of the spec's 10 s for SIGKILL; graceful within 10 s (observed 1-3 s). On a live node, base 819dc283 hands over a SIGKILL with nothing in hand in under 1 s (measured 0.69 s in the smoke), so this order guarantee costs about 11 s there.

Go's default logger gets no instance= prefix (plan 1.7 item 15): the deployed AWS text metric filters are positional and three alarms would stop matching. Pods are told apart by the instance field on every JSON line and the NATS client name (envoy-listener <instance>) on bus lines.
Durable filter is '>' rather than empty (nats-server 2.10 behaviour above).
The address-refusal exception keeps reason delivery_failed (the daemon reads reason as a fixed list); the text 'address not reachable from this listener pod' is in the error log line.
CI job listener-multiprocess runs -run '^Test(TwoPods|TwoBuilds)' so it needs no Postgres; envoy-go already runs the package's untagged tests.
Removed log line 'restored role claims' with the per-process role-revision snapshot it reported (CHANGELOG Removed).
openQuestions: Hard take-over margin: about 12 s against the 15 s test bound; a slow CI runner could approach it.
